# dlasd2

> Merges the two sets of singular values together into a single sorted set, then tries to deflate.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlasd2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasd2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlasd2(
    order,
    NL, NR, SQRE,
    K,
    D, strideD,
    Z, strideZ,
    ALPHA, BETA,
    U, LDU,
    VT, LDVT,
    DSIGMA, strideDSIGMA,
    U2, LDU2,
    VT2, LDVT2,
    IDXP, strideIDXP,
    IDX, strideIDX,
    IDXC, strideIDXC,
    IDXQ, strideIDXQ,
    COLTYP, strideCOLTYP
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`row-major` or `column-major`) |
| `NL` | `integer` | Row dimension of the upper block (>= 1)<br>Rejects `nl < 1` |
| `NR` | `integer` | Row dimension of the lower block (>= 1)<br>Rejects `nr < 1` |
| `SQRE` | `integer` | 0 if lower block is square, 1 if rectangular<br>Rejects `sqre !== 1 && sqre !== 0` |
| `K` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output array; `K[0]` set to dimension of non-deflated matrix |
| `D` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **in/out** · Singular values (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `D` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Updating row vector (length N) |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `Z` |
| `ALPHA` | `number` | Diagonal element associated with the added row |
| `BETA` | `number` | Off-diagonal element associated with the added row |
| `U` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1) × (nl + nr + 1)</sub> | **in/out** · Left singular vectors (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDU` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of U<br>Requires `LDU ≥ nl + nr + 1` |
| `VT` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1 + sqre) × (nl + nr + 1 + sqre)</sub> | **in/out** · Right singular vectors (M x M) |
| ↳ `LDVT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of VT<br>Requires `LDVT ≥ nl + nr + 1 + sqre` |
| `DSIGMA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Output singular values (length N) |
| ↳ `strideDSIGMA` | `integer` | Stride length for `DSIGMA` |
| `U2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1) × (nl + nr + 1)</sub> | **out** · Output left singular vectors copy (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDU2` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of U2<br>Requires `LDU2 ≥ nl + nr + 1` |
| `VT2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1 + sqre) × (nl + nr + 1)</sub> | **out** · Output right singular vectors copy (M x M) |
| ↳ `LDVT2` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of VT2<br>Column-major requires `LDVT2 ≥ nl + nr + 1 + sqre`<br>Row-major requires `LDVT2 ≥ max(1, nl + nr + 1)` |
| `IDXP` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Permutation array (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIDXP` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDXP` |
| `IDX` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Permutation array (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIDX` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDX` |
| `IDXC` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Permutation array (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIDXC` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDXC` |
| `IDXQ` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **in/out** · Permutation array (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIDXQ` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDXQ` |
| `COLTYP` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Column type array (length max(N,4)) |
| ↳ `strideCOLTYP` | `integer` | Stride length for `COLTYP` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `NL`: The row dimension of the upper block. $\mathrm{NL} \ge 1$.
- `NR`: The row dimension of the lower block. $\mathrm{NR} \ge 1$.
- `SQRE`:

  -   `= 0`: the lower block is an `NR`-by-`NR` square matrix.
  -   `= 1`: the lower block is an `NR`-by-(`NR`+1) rectangular matrix.

  The bidiagonal matrix has $N = \mathrm{NL} + \mathrm{NR} + 1$ rows and $M = N + \mathrm{SQRE} \ge N$ columns.
- `K`: Contains the dimension of the non-deflated matrix, This is the order of the related secular equation. $1 \le K \le N$.
- `D`: On entry D contains the singular values of the two submatrices to be combined. On exit D contains the trailing (N-K) updated singular values (those which were deflated) sorted into increasing order.
- `Z`: On exit Z contains the updating row vector in the secular equation.
- `ALPHA`: Contains the diagonal element associated with the added row.
- `BETA`: Contains the off-diagonal element associated with the added row.
- `U`: On entry U contains the left singular vectors of two submatrices in the two square blocks with corners at (1,1), (`NL`, `NL`), and (`NL`+2, `NL`+2), (N,N). On exit U contains the trailing (N-K) updated left singular vectors (those which were deflated) in its last N-K columns.
- `VT`: On entry $\mathrm{VT}^T$ contains the right singular vectors of two submatrices in the two square blocks with corners at (1,1), (`NL`+1, `NL`+1), and (`NL`+2, `NL`+2), (M,M). On exit $\mathrm{VT}^T$ contains the trailing (N-K) updated right singular vectors (those which were deflated) in its last N-K columns. In case `SQRE =1`, the last row of `VT` spans the right null space.
- `DSIGMA`: Contains a copy of the diagonal elements (K-1 singular values and one zero) in the secular equation.
- `U2`: Contains a copy of the first K-1 left singular vectors which will be used by DLASD3 in a matrix multiply (DGEMM) to solve for the new left singular vectors. `U2` is arranged into four blocks. The first block contains a column with 1 at `NL`+1 and zero everywhere else; the second block contains non-zero entries only at and above `NL`; the third contains non-zero entries only below `NL`+1; and the fourth is dense.
- `VT2`: $\mathrm{VT2}^T$ contains a copy of the first K right singular vectors which will be used by DLASD3 in a matrix multiply (DGEMM) to solve for the new right singular vectors. `VT2` is arranged into three blocks. The first block contains a row that corresponds to the special 0 diagonal element in SIGMA; the second block contains non-zeros only at and before `NL` +1; the third block contains non-zeros only at and after `NL` +2.
- `IDXP`: This will contain the permutation used to place deflated values of D at the end of the array. On output `IDXP(2:K)` points to the nondeflated D-values and `IDXP(K+1:N)` points to the deflated singular values.
- `IDX`: This will contain the permutation used to sort the contents of D into ascending order.
- `IDXC`: This will contain the permutation used to arrange the columns of the deflated U matrix into three groups: the first group contains non-zero entries only at and above `NL`, the second contains non-zero entries only below `NL`+2, and the third is dense.
- `IDXQ`: This contains the permutation which separately sorts the two sub-problems in D into ascending order. Note that entries in the first hlaf of this permutation must first be moved one position backward; and entries in the second half must first have `NL`+1 added to their values.
- `COLTYP`: As workspace, this will contain a label which will indicate which of the following types a column in the `U2` matrix or a row in the `VT2` matrix is: 1 : non-zero in the upper half only 2 : non-zero in the lower half only 3 : dense 4 : deflated

  On exit, it is an array of dimension 4, with `COLTYP(I)` being the dimension of the I-th type columns.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `NL < 1`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `NR < 1`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `SQRE !== 1 && SQRE !== 0`)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `NL + NR + 1`
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `NL + NR + 1 + SQRE`
- `RangeError` nineteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `NL + NR + 1`
- `RangeError` twenty-first argument must be greater than or equal to `NL + NR + 1 + SQRE` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-first argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, NL + NR + 1 )` (row-major)

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlasd2.strided(
    nl, nr, sqre,
    K,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    z, strideZ, offsetZ,
    alpha, beta,
    U, strideU1,
    strideU2,
    offsetU,
    VT, strideVT1,
    strideVT2,
    offsetVT,
    DSIGMA, strideDSIGMA, offsetDSIGMA,
    U2, strideU21, strideU22, offsetU2,
    VT2, strideVT21, strideVT22, offsetVT2,
    IDXP, strideIDXP, offsetIDXP,
    IDX, strideIDX, offsetIDX,
    IDXC, strideIDXC, offsetIDXC,
    IDXQ, strideIDXQ, offsetIDXQ,
    COLTYP, strideCOLTYP, offsetCOLTYP
) → integer
```

Merge two sets of singular values in bidiagonal SVD divide and conquer.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `nl` | `integer` | The row dimension of the upper block.<br>Rejects `nl < 1` |
| `nr` | `integer` | The row dimension of the lower block.<br>Rejects `nr < 1` |
| `sqre` | `integer` | = 0: the lower block is an NR-by-NR square matrix. = 1: the lower block is an NR-by-(NR+1) rectangular matrix.<br>Rejects `sqre !== 1 && sqre !== 0` |
| `K` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output array; `K[0]` set to dimension of non-deflated matrix |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `z` |
| `alpha` | `number` | Scalar constant |
| `beta` | `number` | Scalar constant |
| `U` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1) × (nl + nr + 1)</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideU1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `U` |
| ↳ `strideU2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `U` |
| ↳ `offsetU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `U` |
| `VT` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1 + sqre) × (nl + nr + 1 + sqre)</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVT1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `VT` |
| ↳ `strideVT2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `VT` |
| ↳ `offsetVT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `VT` |
| `DSIGMA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideDSIGMA` | `integer` | Stride length for `DSIGMA` |
| ↳ `offsetDSIGMA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DSIGMA` |
| `U2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1) × (nl + nr + 1)</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideU21` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `U2` |
| ↳ `strideU22` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `U2` |
| ↳ `offsetU2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `U2` |
| `VT2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(nl + nr + 1 + sqre) × (nl + nr + 1)</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVT21` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `VT2` |
| ↳ `strideVT22` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `VT2` |
| ↳ `offsetVT2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `VT2` |
| `IDXP` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideIDXP` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDXP` |
| ↳ `offsetIDXP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IDXP` |
| `IDX` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideIDX` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDX` |
| ↳ `offsetIDX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IDX` |
| `IDXC` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideIDXC` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDXC` |
| ↳ `offsetIDXC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IDXC` |
| `IDXQ` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideIDXQ` | `integer` | Stride length for `IDXQ` |
| ↳ `offsetIDXQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IDXQ` |
| `COLTYP` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length nl + nr + 1</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideCOLTYP` | `integer` | Stride length for `COLTYP` |
| ↳ `offsetCOLTYP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `COLTYP` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `nl`: The row dimension of the upper block. $\mathrm{NL} \ge 1$.
- `nr`: The row dimension of the lower block. $\mathrm{NR} \ge 1$.
- `sqre`:

  -   `= 0`: the lower block is an `NR`-by-`NR` square matrix.
  -   `= 1`: the lower block is an `NR`-by-(`NR`+1) rectangular matrix.

  The bidiagonal matrix has $N = \mathrm{NL} + \mathrm{NR} + 1$ rows and $M = N + \mathrm{SQRE} \ge N$ columns.
- `K`: Contains the dimension of the non-deflated matrix, This is the order of the related secular equation. $1 \le K \le N$.
- `d`: On entry D contains the singular values of the two submatrices to be combined. On exit D contains the trailing (N-K) updated singular values (those which were deflated) sorted into increasing order.
- `z`: On exit Z contains the updating row vector in the secular equation.
- `alpha`: Contains the diagonal element associated with the added row.
- `beta`: Contains the off-diagonal element associated with the added row.
- `U`: On entry U contains the left singular vectors of two submatrices in the two square blocks with corners at (1,1), (`NL`, `NL`), and (`NL`+2, `NL`+2), (N,N). On exit U contains the trailing (N-K) updated left singular vectors (those which were deflated) in its last N-K columns.
- `VT`: On entry $\mathrm{VT}^T$ contains the right singular vectors of two submatrices in the two square blocks with corners at (1,1), (`NL`+1, `NL`+1), and (`NL`+2, `NL`+2), (M,M). On exit $\mathrm{VT}^T$ contains the trailing (N-K) updated right singular vectors (those which were deflated) in its last N-K columns. In case `SQRE =1`, the last row of `VT` spans the right null space.
- `DSIGMA`: Contains a copy of the diagonal elements (K-1 singular values and one zero) in the secular equation.
- `U2`: Contains a copy of the first K-1 left singular vectors which will be used by DLASD3 in a matrix multiply (DGEMM) to solve for the new left singular vectors. `U2` is arranged into four blocks. The first block contains a column with 1 at `NL`+1 and zero everywhere else; the second block contains non-zero entries only at and above `NL`; the third contains non-zero entries only below `NL`+1; and the fourth is dense.
- `VT2`: $\mathrm{VT2}^T$ contains a copy of the first K right singular vectors which will be used by DLASD3 in a matrix multiply (DGEMM) to solve for the new right singular vectors. `VT2` is arranged into three blocks. The first block contains a row that corresponds to the special 0 diagonal element in SIGMA; the second block contains non-zeros only at and before `NL` +1; the third block contains non-zeros only at and after `NL` +2.
- `IDXP`: This will contain the permutation used to place deflated values of D at the end of the array. On output `IDXP(2:K)` points to the nondeflated D-values and `IDXP(K+1:N)` points to the deflated singular values.
- `IDX`: This will contain the permutation used to sort the contents of D into ascending order.
- `IDXC`: This will contain the permutation used to arrange the columns of the deflated U matrix into three groups: the first group contains non-zero entries only at and above `NL`, the second contains non-zero entries only below `NL`+2, and the third is dense.
- `IDXQ`: This contains the permutation which separately sorts the two sub-problems in D into ascending order. Note that entries in the first hlaf of this permutation must first be moved one position backward; and entries in the second half must first have `NL`+1 added to their values.
- `COLTYP`: As workspace, this will contain a label which will indicate which of the following types a column in the `U2` matrix or a row in the `VT2` matrix is: 1 : non-zero in the upper half only 2 : non-zero in the lower half only 3 : dense 4 : deflated

  On exit, it is an array of dimension 4, with `COLTYP(I)` being the dimension of the I-th type columns.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument is invalid (rejected when `nl < 1`)
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `nr < 1`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `sqre !== 1 && sqre !== 0`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

## Notes

-   `dlasd2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLASD2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlasd2.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlasd2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasd2';

// Merge two upper bidiagonal blocks (NL = NR = 2, SQRE = 0) with identity singular vectors:
const NL = 2;
const NR = 2;
const SQRE = 0;
const N = NL + NR + 1;
const M = N + SQRE;

/**
* Returns an `n`-by-`n` identity matrix.
*
* @private
* @param {PositiveInteger} n - order
* @returns {Float64Array} identity matrix
*/
function eye( n ) {
	const out = new Float64Array( n * n );
	let i;
	for ( i = 0; i < n; i++ ) {
		out[ ( i * n ) + i ] = 1.0;
	}
	return out;
}

let D = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 3.0, 0.0, 2.0, 4.0 ] );
let Z = new Float64Array( M );
let U = eye( N );
let VT = eye( M );
let IDXQ = new Int32Array( [ 1, 2, 0, 1, 2 ] ); // sorting permutations of each block (1-based)
const K = new Int32Array( 1 );
const DSIGMA = new Float64Array( N );
const U2 = new Float64Array( N * N );
const VT2 = new Float64Array( M * M );
const IDXP = new Int32Array( N );
const IDX = new Int32Array( N );
const IDXC = new Int32Array( N );
const COLTYP = new Int32Array( Math.max( N, 4 ) );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dlasd2( 'column-major', NL, NR, SQRE, K, D, 1, Z, 1, 0.5, 0.7, U, N, VT, M, DSIGMA, 1, U2, N, VT2, M, IDXP, 1, IDX, 1, IDXC, 1, IDXQ, 1, COLTYP, 1 );
console.log( info, K[ 0 ], DSIGMA, Z ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
D = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 3.0, 0.0, 2.0, 4.0 ] );
Z = new Float64Array( M );
U = eye( N );
VT = eye( M );
IDXQ = new Int32Array( [ 1, 2, 0, 1, 2 ] );
info = dlasd2.strided( NL, NR, SQRE, K, D, 1, 0, Z, 1, 0, 0.5, 0.7, U, 1, N, 0, VT, 1, M, 0, DSIGMA, 1, 0, U2, 1, N, 0, VT2, 1, M, 0, IDXP, 1, 0, IDX, 1, 0, IDXC, 1, 0, IDXQ, 1, 0, COLTYP, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, K[ 0 ], DSIGMA, Z ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLASD2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLASD2 merges the two sets of singular values together into a single sorted set. Then it tries to deflate the size of the problem. There are two ways in which deflation can occur: when two or more singular values are close together or if there is a tiny entry in the Z vector. For each such occurrence the order of the related secular equation problem is reduced by one.

DLASD2 is called from DLASD1.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
